s: Angeline Stickney writes poetry (during college)
q: To complete this study of Angeline Stickney’s college writings, it is necessary, though somewhat painful, to quote specimens of her poetry.

s: Ruth memorizes poem (preserving it when no manuscript existed)
q: its preservation being due to the loving admiration of Ruth Stickney, who memorized it:

s: Asaph Hall is a carpenter (before becoming an astronomer)
q: Asaph Hall, carpenter, and afterwards astronomer, came of excellent family.

s: Asaph Hall is a astronomer (after working as a carpenter)
q: Asaph Hall, carpenter, and afterwards astronomer, came of excellent family.

s: Asaph Hall is descended from John Hall (of Wallingford, Connecticut)
q: He was descended from John Hall, of Wallingford, Conn., who served in the Pequot War.

s: Angeline Stickney is a student (at Central College)
q: I am glad that I am here because I love this institution.

s: Asaph Hall 1st served in the American Revolution (as captain of Connecticut militia)
q: His grandfather, Asaph Hall 1st, saw service in the Revolution as captain of Connecticut militia.

s: Angeline Stickney is a Puritan (in religious sentiment and earnestness)
q: They are Puritanism brought down to the nineteenth century—solemn, absurd, almost maudlin in their religious sentimentality, and yet deeply earnest and at times noble.

s: Asaph Hall died in Georgia (while selling clocks)
q: His inheritance rapidly slipped away; and in 1842 he died in Georgia, where he was selling clocks, manufactured in his Goshen factory.

s: Angeline Stickney practices rigid economy (in preserving and reusing manuscripts)
q: The manuscripts upon which these literary productions are recorded are worn, creased, stained, torn and covered with writing—bearing witness to the rigid economy practiced by the writer.

s: Angeline Stickney has careful penmanship (with clearly formed letters)
q: The penmanship is careful, every letter clearly formed, for Angeline Stickney was not one of those vain persons who imagine that slovenly handwriting is a mark of genius.

s: New York Central College is a Alma Mater (of Angeline Stickney)
q: I bade adieu to my fellow students here, and took the farewell look of the loved Alma Mater, Central College.

s: New York Central College welcomes all (regardless of tongue or color)
q: I love the spirit that welcomes all to its halls, those of every tongue, and of every hue, which admits of “no rights exclusive,”

s: New York Central College holds out knowledge (universally and without exclusive rights)
q: which holds out the cup of knowledge in it’s crystal brightness for all to quaff;

s: Asaph Hall has physical inheritance from Hannah (Palmer) Hall (splendid physique)
q: To her Asaph Hall 3rd owed in large measure his splendid physique; and who can say whether his mental powers were inherited from father or mother?

s: Asaph Hall participates in cheese production and sale (with his mother and siblings; ten thousand pounds produced and sold in one year)
q: During one of these years they made and sold ten thousand pounds of cheese, at six cents a pound.

s: Asaph Hall serves apprenticeship in carpentry (three years)

q: Now at the age of twenty-four or twenty-five Asaph Hall 3rd only began serious study.

s: Asaph Hall is a scholar (admired by fellow-students and encouraged by teachers)
q: His ability as a scholar called forth the admiration of fellow-students and the encouragement of teachers.

s: education is subject to the conventional theory of education (as criticized in the text)
q: Massachusetts educators would have us believe that a young man of twenty-five should have spent nine years in primary and grammar schools, four years more in a high school, four years more at college, and three years more in some professional school.

s: Brünnow recognizes as disciple Asaph Hall (worthy disciple)
q: The astronomer Brünnow, buried in the wilds of Michigan, far from his beloved Germany, recognized in this American youth a worthy disciple

s: Asaph Hall is eldest child of Hannah (Palmer) Hall (eldest of six children)
q: Asaph Hall 3rd, born October 15, 1829, was the eldest of six children.

s: Dr. Benjamin Apthorp Gould adopts into scientific family Asaph Hall
q: Dr. Benjamin Apthorp Gould, father of American astronomy, promptly adopted Asaph Hall into his scientific family.

s: Asaph Hall is a skilled and conscientious workman (after eight years of carpentry)
q: He had spent eight years at carpenter work; three years as an apprentice and five years as a journeyman, and he was a skilful and conscientious workman.

s: Asaph Hall has experience in carpentry (eight years: three as apprentice and five as journeyman)
q: He had spent eight years at carpenter work; three years as an apprentice and five years as a journeyman

s: Asaph Hall constructs the roof of a house (scientifically, using principles of projection)
q: And yet it was Asaph Hall who showed his fellow carpenters how to construct the roof of a house scientifically.

s: Asaph Hall solves the problem of constructing a house roof (by the principles of projection)
q: And yet it was Asaph Hall who showed his fellow carpenters how to construct the roof of a house scientifically. “Cut and try” was their rule; and if the end of a joist was spoilt by too frequent application of the rule, they took another joist. But the young carpenter knew the thing could be done right the first time; and so, without the aid of text-book or instructor, he worked the problem out, by the principles of projection.

s: the problem of constructing a house roof uses the principles of projection
q: he worked the problem out, by the principles of projection.

s: Asaph Hall builds houses built by Asaph Hall (well-built houses in Connecticut and Massachusetts)
q: Monuments of his handiwork, in the shape of well-built houses, are to be seen in Connecticut and Massachusetts to this day.

s: Peter Bogart is employer of Asaph Hall (carpentry boss)
q: his boss, old Peter Bogart, used to say with a twinkle in his eye, that of all the men in his employ, Asaph Hall was the only one who didn’t know more than Peter Bogart.

s: Asaph Hall aspires to be architect (after proving himself more than a carpenter)
q: To himself the incident meant much, for he had proved himself more than a carpenter. His ambition was aroused, and he resolved to become an architect.

s: Asaph Hall's journey to McGrawville destination McGrawville (in 1854)
q: In 1854 he set out for McGrawville thinking that by the system of manual labor there advertised he could earn his way as he studied.

q: When the stage rolled into town, whom should he see but Angeline Stickney, dressed in her “bloomer” costume!

s: the bloomer costume is worn by Angeline Stickney
q: Angeline Stickney, dressed in her “bloomer” costume!

s: Hannah (Palmer) Hall is mother of Asaph Hall
q: Her house was always home to him; and when cold weather put a stop to carpentry, he returned thither to help tend cattle or to hunt gray squirrels.

s: marriage unites people of Christianity (according to President Eliot's view)
q: President Eliot of Harvard University is quoted as saying that marriage ought to unite two persons of the same religious faith: otherwise it is likely to prove unhappy.

s: Angeline Stickney has health (feeble and seriously impaired during courtship)
q: He, wise lover, could distinguish between sins of the stomach and sins of the heart, and risked the hereditary taint pertaining to the former—and this although she emphasized the danger by breaking down and becoming a pitiable invalid

s: Angeline Stickney writes letters (to Asaph Hall during courtship)
q: Some words of endearment are preserved in their old letters—but these, gentle reader, are none of your business.

s: Angeline Stickney holds views about women’s usefulness (favoring earnest, useful work over fashionable display)
q: I could not help contrasting those ladies of fashion with the earnest, noble, working women who stood up there in that Convention, and with words of eloquence urged upon their sisters the importance of awaking to usefulness.

s: Angeline Stickney possesses knowledge of surveying (unusually for a woman of her time)
q: It seems the surveyor of the neighborhood was surprised to find a woman who understood his business.

s: Angeline Stickney writes poem (during courtship)
q: In the same letter she speaks about lengthening a poem, so that the time occupied in reading it was about twenty minutes.

s: Angeline Stickney encourages prayer-meeting (as part of her religious concern for Asaph Hall)
q: Did you go to the prayer-meeting last evening? It seemed to me that you were there.

s: Angeline Stickney believes in the life beyond the grave (and urges Asaph Hall to prepare for it)
q: You must take some time, Love, to think of the life beyond the grave.

s: Asaph Hall is a carpenter (before and during courtship)
q: But Dan Cupid contrived to have him pursue a course in geometry taught by Miss Stickney; and, to make it all the merrier, entangled him in a plot to down the teacher by asking hard questions.

s: Asaph Hall is outside Christianity (outside the pale of any religious sect)

q: And so Asaph Hall studied astronomy under the famous Brünnow, and French under Fasquelle.

q: And he used to carry his frail wife on his back across the fields to hunt wild flowers.

s: courtship involves geometry (through Asaph Hall's course with Angeline Stickney)
q: But Dan Cupid contrived to have him pursue a course in geometry taught by Miss Stickney; and, to make it all the merrier, entangled him in a plot to down the teacher by asking hard questions.

s: courtship leads to a pair of happy lovers
q: The teacher did not down, admiration took the place of mischief, and Cupid smiled upon a pair of happy lovers.

s: engagement ring is worn by Angeline Stickney (for twenty years despite her Puritanical protest)
q: But he went about to get the engagement ring, which, in spite of a Puritanical protest against such adornment, was faithfully worn for twenty years.

s: marriage of Angeline Stickney and Asaph Hall occurs in 1856 (on a Monday morning after a visit to Elder Bright)
q: We were married Monday morning, and started for this place in the afternoon.

s: marriage of Angeline Stickney and Asaph Hall is fortunate (described as infinitely more fortunate than Angeline Stickney’s friend’s marriage)
q: And her marriage was infinitely more fortunate than her friend’s.

s: marriage of Angeline Stickney and Asaph Hall takes place on Monday morning
q: Mr. Hall and I went to Elder Bright’s and staid over Sunday. We were married Monday morning, and started for this place in the afternoon. Mr. Hall came here for the purpose of pursuing his studies.

s: Angeline Stickney is a Baptist (as a sincere adherent)
q: Angeline Stickney, like her girl friend, was a sincere Baptist.

s: marriage of Angeline Stickney and Asaph Hall is supported by mutual encouragement (as described by Asaph Hall before the marriage)
q: At least, I am sure that we shall feel stronger, and better fitted to act an honorable part in life, when we are living together, and encouraging each other, than we could otherwise.

s: Angeline Stickney joined the church (at the age of sixteen)
q: Had joined the church at the age of sixteen.

s: Angeline Stickney marries Asaph Hall (in a marriage described as fortunate)
q: But she married Asaph Hall, who was outside the pale of any religious sect, disbelieved in woman-suffrage, wasted little sympathy on <DW64>s, and played cards! And her marriage was infinitely more fortunate than her friend’s.

s: Angeline Stickney attempts to convert Asaph Hall (partially succeeding before he converted her)
q: To be sure she labored to convert her splendid Pagan, and partially succeeded; but in the end he converted her, till the Unitarian church itself was too narrow for her.

s: Angeline Stickney is converted by Asaph Hall (eventually and religiously)
q: To be sure she labored to convert her splendid Pagan, and partially succeeded; but in the end he converted her, till the Unitarian church itself was too narrow for her.

s: Angeline Stickney wears the bloomer costume (solemnly, before her courtship with Asaph Hall)
q: No doubt the little god scored a point when Asaph Hall saw Angeline Stickney solemnly parading in the “bloomer” costume.

s: Angeline Stickney discloses Theophilus Stickney (before becoming engaged to Asaph Hall)
q: It was characteristic of her that before she became engaged to marry she told Asaph Hall all about her father.
